html:
Séga is the music and dance of the Mascarene Islands, created by enslaved Africans and Malagasy on Mauritius and Réunion, sung in Creole to the beat of a goatskin frame drum called the ravanne.

On the plantations it was sung at night around fires, with songs of hardship, love and mockery of masters, and dancers swaying their hips. It was looked down on by the colonial elite and the planters.

In the 20th century singers such as Ti Frère brought it to radio and stages, and it mixed with reggae into seggae in the 1980s. UNESCO listed traditional Mauritian séga as world heritage in 2014. It is the shared music of all communities in Mauritius, and is sung in Mauritian Creole, the language of the islands.
sum: Séga is the music and dance of the Mascarene Islands, created by enslaved Africans and Malagasy on Mauritius and Réunion, sung in Creole to the beat of a goatskin frame drum called the ravanne.
